claims.text: Machine-learning models trained on thermodynamic and structural data can accurately and efficiently predict fusion and liquid-phase properties across the HEA family.
Machine-learning models will outperform CALPHAD and rule-of-mixtures approaches in both speed and accuracy for unexplored HEA compositions.
Atomic radii, electronegativity, mixing entropy, lattice distortion, and compositional features are informative inputs for predicting HEA fusion and liquid properties.
The ML model learns nonlinear correlations between structural or compositional features and thermodynamic properties.
Patterns in existing experimental and computational data allow the model to generalize to new HEA compositions.
Within the training domain, melting-temperature predictions will have a mean absolute error below 50 K.
Within the training domain, predicted enthalpies of fusion will have errors below 10%.
Within the training domain, predicted entropies of fusion will have errors below 10%.
Within the training domain, predicted volume changes at melting will have errors below 10%.
Liquid-phase heat capacity and viscosity will be predicted within 15% error.
ML prediction will be orders of magnitude faster than first-principles or CALPHAD calculations.
Traditional CALPHAD and rule-of-mixtures approaches typically have melting-temperature mean absolute errors above 100 K.
Traditional CALPHAD and rule-of-mixtures approaches typically have errors above 15% for fusion properties.
Traditional CALPHAD and rule-of-mixtures approaches require more computational time per composition than the proposed ML approach.
The approach is applicable to HEAs containing three to seven principal elements in equiatomic or near-equiatomic ratios when those compositions and structures are represented by the training data.
The stated predictions apply under ambient pressure and standard melting conditions.
Extrapolation to radically different compositions, intermetallic phases, or amorphous alloys may produce unreliable predictions.
Prediction accuracy depends on the quality and diversity of the training data.
Prediction uncertainty increases for compositions far from the training domain.
Liquid-phase properties are less well represented in existing databases, causing greater uncertainty in their predictions.

contradictions.description: The headline claim describes performance across the HEA family and for unexplored compositions, whereas the conditions and boundary restrict applicability to compositions and structural types represented in the training domain.
